reference.title: Scenario 3 — Table with no header row
reference.shortdesc: Consider a table where the author has not formatted the first row as a header

section.p: Consider a table where the author has not formatted the first row as a header — all rows contain data.

row.entry: [Row]: server-01 | 192.168.1.10 | Active [Row]: server-02 | 192.168.1.11 | Standby [Row]: server-03 | 192.168.1.12 | Active

entry.codeblock: <simpletable> <sthead> <!-- First data row promoted as header --> <stentry>server-01</stentry> <stentry>192.168.1.10</stentry> <stentry>Active</stentry> </sthead> <strow> <stentry>server-02</stentry> <stentry>192.168.1.11</stentry> <stentry>Standby</stentry> </strow> <strow> <stentry>server-03</stentry> <stentry>192.168.1.12</stentry> <stentry>Active</stentry> </strow> </simpletable>

section.p: Result:The converter assumes that the first row of every Word table represents the header row. Since no actual header exists, the converter promotes the first data row into <sthead>. Always include a descriptive header row in Word tables.
